title: Suspected CTCL — Initial Workup Pathway
subtitle: History → Examination → Biopsy → Staging labs and imaging

items.label: Duration and chronicity of skin rash
items.detail: CTCL is notorious for diagnostic delay (median 4-6 years from symptom onset). Ask about prior diagnoses of eczema, psoriasis, or contact dermatitis that failed appropriate treatment.

items.label: Refractoriness to potent topical corticosteroids
items.detail: Chronic patches or plaques that persist despite multiple courses of class I-II topical steroids are a classic red flag. Inquire specifically about the number and duration of prior steroid trials.

items.label: Distribution of lesions — sun-protected areas, bathing-suit pattern
items.detail: Early MF classically affects the hips, buttocks, lower trunk, and inner thighs — areas covered by a bathing suit. Sun-exposed distribution is less typical.

items.label: Symptoms: pruritus (often severe), burning, or pain
Prior biopsies and pathology reports — review all previous histology
B symptoms: unexplained fever, night sweats, weight loss >10%
items.detail: Constitutional symptoms suggest advanced systemic disease. Document carefully as they affect staging and management.

items.label: Atypical eczema features: onset in adulthood, waxing/waning course, large poikilodermatous patches
Medications: recent new drugs, immunosuppressants (may mask or mimic CTCL)
Personal or family history of lymphoma or other hematologic malignancies
Full body skin examination with body surface area (BSA) mapping
items.detail: Use the rule-of-nines or palmar method. Document the type (patch, plaque, tumor, erythroderma) and anatomical distribution of all lesions. Photograph and map for longitudinal tracking.

items.label: Identify patch vs. plaque vs. tumor morphology
items.detail: Patches are flat, non-indurated areas with fine scale or wrinkled texture. Plaques are indurated and elevated. Tumors are solid nodules >1 cm in depth. Classification drives T-staging.

items.label: Assess for erythroderma (T4): erythema involving ≥80% BSA
items.detail: Erythrodermic MF or Sézary syndrome. Patients may have desquamation, edema, ectropion, and leonine facies. Requires blood staging (Sézary count, flow cytometry).

items.label: Palpate all nodal basins: cervical, axillary, inguinal, femoral
items.detail: Note size, consistency, mobility. Nodes >1.5 cm or firm/fixed are clinically abnormal. Adenopathy directly affects N staging.

items.label: Hepatosplenomegaly assessment (abdominal palpation, percussion)
Ophthalmologic review if periorbital or facial involvement suspected
Dermoscopy (trichoscopy if folliculotropic MF suspected)
items.detail: Folliculotropic MF may show follicular plugging, perifollicular erythema, and alopecia without obvious scale. Dermoscopy aids in identifying follicular involvement.

items.label: Photo-document all lesions at baseline
Take multiple (at least 2) deep punch biopsies from most indurated, active lesion edges
items.detail: Single biopsy is insufficient — diagnostic yield improves with multiple specimens from different sites. Use 4mm punch minimum. Avoid scarred, excoriated, or secondarily infected areas.

items.label: Submit for routine H&E histopathology: evaluate epidermotropism and Pautrier microabscesses
items.detail: Pautrier microabscesses (intraepidermal clusters of atypical lymphocytes) are pathognomonic but seen in only ~10-30% of cases. Band-like lymphocytic infiltrate with epidermotropism is the hallmark.

items.label: Immunohistochemistry panel: CD3, CD4, CD7, CD8, CD20, CD30, CD56
items.detail: Classic MF: CD3+, CD4+, CD7 loss (CD7- in >50% of tumor cells is supportive), CD8-, CD30 variable. Loss of pan-T markers (CD2, CD5, CD7) increases specificity. CD30+ (≥10%) predicts response to brentuximab vedotin.

items.label: T-cell receptor (TCR) gene rearrangement by PCR or next-generation sequencing
items.detail: Clonal TCR-gamma rearrangement supports diagnosis but is not pathognomonic (benign inflammatory dermatoses can show clonality). Correlate with histology and clinical picture. Useful for comparing blood and skin clones.

items.label: If folliculotropic MF suspected: request levels/serial sections to identify follicular involvement
items.branchIf: Follicular papules, alopecia, or comedone-like lesions present

items.label: Repeat biopsy if initial is non-diagnostic — serial biopsies over time may be required
items.detail: Early CTCL frequently requires multiple biopsies over months to years before a definitive diagnosis can be established. The diagnosis should integrate clinical, histological, immunophenotypic, and molecular data.

items.label: CBC with manual differential — Sézary cell count
items.detail: Request manual differential to identify atypical lymphocytes (Sézary cells: cerebriform nucleus). Sézary cells >1000/mcL define B2 blood involvement. Routine CBC differentials may miss these cells.

items.label: Peripheral blood flow cytometry: CD4/CD8 ratio, CD4+CD7-, CD4+CD26-
items.detail: CD4:CD8 ratio >10, CD4+CD7- >40%, or CD4+CD26- >30% each define B2 (high-burden) blood involvement. Order if there is erythroderma, B symptoms, or clinical suspicion for Sézary syndrome.

items.label: Peripheral blood TCR clonality — compare to skin clone
items.detail: Identical TCR clone in blood and skin strongly supports Sézary syndrome when combined with B2 criteria. Submit blood and skin to the same laboratory for direct comparison.

items.label: Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) — correlates with tumor burden
Comprehensive metabolic panel, uric acid, beta-2 microglobulin
CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis with contrast
items.detail: Recommended for all patients with T2 or higher disease, palpable adenopathy, or B symptoms. Assess lymph node size, hepatosplenomegaly, and visceral involvement. PET-CT may replace CT in some centers.
items.branchIf: T2, T3, T4, or any lymphadenopathy

items.label: PET-CT if high-stage or aggressive disease suspected
items.detail: PET-CT improves sensitivity for nodal and visceral involvement compared to CT alone. Particularly useful for identifying the optimal biopsy site and assessing treatment response.
items.branchIf: Stage IIB or higher, or rapid clinical progression

items.label: Lymph node biopsy of most abnormal node if palpable adenopathy or CT-enlarged nodes present
items.detail: Preferentially excise the most abnormal node. Core needle biopsy is acceptable if excision is not feasible. Send for histology, flow cytometry, and TCR clonality. Grade per Dutch/NCI system (N1-N4).
